parsed.why: Sodomy sections (up to 14 years) remain on the books but are unenforced, with no reported prosecutions or documented anti-trans targeting, and a recognised third-gender cultural role. Thin, decade-old data, no protections or recourse — a step below acceptance-with-protections.

Same-sex conduct criminalised and actively enforced (arrests, convictions, mass 2023 arrests), president urging stoning and calling it a licence to kill, police extortion, torture and killings amid state crisis, no protection or recourse. Gender-nonconforming visitors are squarely exposed.

No criminalisation, facilities access protected, working courts that convicted a trans woman's murderer, anti-discrimination covering gender identity, strong institutional record and rising acceptance. Gaps: no gender-identity hate-crime law, high local avoidance, one prosecuted 2022 killing.

State-imposed exposures with no working remedy: prison placement by birth sex with isolation and strip searches (recurring oversight findings), border document friction, 64% trans discrimination. Strong laws and prosecution of attackers partly offset, but oversight findings recur unremedied.

Universal border exposure — X markers ended, mismatched documents risk refusal and lifetime fraud ineligibility — plus facility bans in many states, a bathroom-arrest precedent, custody conversion practices, and state framing of pro-trans groups as extremist. Allied travel advisories followed.
